Action Plan:
1. Right knee pain/clicking: continue ice therapy, temporarily reduce running mileage, start prescribed stronger NSAID (drug, dose/route/frequency not documented) with food; discontinue concurrent ibuprofen use.
2. Arrange referral to physiotherapy for detailed knee examination; physiotherapist to advise on rehabilitation exercises and determine need for imaging (e.g., MRI) for possible cartilage or ligament injury.
3. Provide safety-net advice: present to urgent care or call back if knee develops persistent swelling, heat, redness, fever, locking, or inability to fully bend/straighten.
4. Intermittent right toe tingling/leg swelling: observe; return for review if paresthesia or edema recurs or worsens.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• 43-year-old female marathon trainee.  
• Presenting complaint: 2-week history of progressive right knee pain and clicking during/after runs ≥20 min (~3 mi); pain sometimes forces cessation of running.  
• Clicking also noted during abdominal workouts requiring knee flexion/extension.  
• Initial mild swelling after first painful run resolved with ice; currently no swelling or pain at rest.  
• Occasional tingling in right toes after a run; single episode, resolved.  
• No giving way, locking, stair difficulty, or limitations in daily walking.  
• Past injury: ice-hockey fall with large bruise to knee “a few months ago,” fully recovered.  
• Past medical history: farsightedness (post-LASIK), remote severe UTI; no chronic illnesses reported.  
• Medications: ibuprofen 400 mg PRN; Aleve (naproxen, dose/route/frequency not documented) PRN; vitamin D (dose not documented); melatonin PRN; Xanax PRN for insomnia (dose/route/frequency not documented); occasional cannabis joint.  
• Allergies: not stated.  
• Social: physically active; training 4–8 mi runs; gym several times weekly; occasional cannabis use.

Objective:
(Telehealth – no direct examination)  
• Patient reports current full range of motion; able to fully flex and extend knee.  
• No visible swelling on video at time of consult (per patient report).  
• No redness, heat, or deformity reported.  
• No vitals or in-office tests performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Right knee pain/clicking  
   - Assessment: Likely overuse injury/patellofemoral pain syndrome vs meniscal or ligamentous pathology.  
   - Differential: Meniscal tear, ACL/PCL strain, early osteoarthritis.  
   - Investigations planned: Deferred; imaging (MRI) if persistent symptoms after physiotherapy assessment.  
   - Treatment planned: Continue ice; reduce running; prescribe stronger NSAID (name/dose not documented) with food; avoid concurrent ibuprofen.  
   - Relevant referrals: Physiotherapy for comprehensive knee assessment and rehabilitation program.

2. Intermittent right toe tingling & episodic lower-leg swelling  
   - Assessment: Exercise-related transient paresthesia/edema; currently resolved.  
   - Differential: Nerve entrapment, vascular insufficiency, early compartment syndrome (unlikely).  
   - Investigations planned: None at present; review if recurrent.  
   - Treatment planned: Observation; patient education on monitoring.  
   - Relevant referrals: None at this stage.

Quality checks:
• Missing elements: Allergies not documented; no vital signs; medication doses/frequencies for several agents unspecified.  
• Internal conflicts: Initial mention “both knees” vs later clarification pain only in right knee—conflict noted, right knee primary.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor conversational overlaps but clinically adequate.
